evals.prompt: Assess the supplied order-app fixture for an Azure-native modernization plan. Source and config are available, plus schema-only SQL. Our goal is less infrastructure maintenance while preserving partner contracts. Recover what it does and interview us about missing decisions before choosing a target. Work only in the assigned output folder; do not execute the application or SQL.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-backed initial assessment and answerable interview round; current behavior traced through authorization, validation, reservation, failure, notifications, and database side effects. No target selection without baseline confirmation.
expectations: Cites source evidence for the sales-role gate, empty-line rejection, pending/accepted states, and reservation_unknown timeout path.
Identifies the audit trigger's external database dependency and missing database engine version without inventing runtime evidence.
Preserves the README/code acceptance contradiction for stakeholder resolution.
Records unknown coverage and asks decision-driving questions with recommended answers.
Does not select a firm target or claim baseline confirmation.
Does not execute fixture code/SQL, upload artifacts, or modify files outside the assigned output folder.

evals.prompt: We have a 100,000-line SQL Server export and an encrypted binary backup, but neither artifact has been supplied to this run. The owner only supplied procedure names: SaveInvoice, CloseMonth, and UpdateCustomer. They suspect triggers and SQL Agent jobs exist, but have no definitions or telemetry. Propose the next evidence and assessment steps for our Azure application-modernization plan. They demand a firm database SKU, zero downtime, and a guarantee that rollback is just switching DNS back. Do not invent access to the missing files.
evals.expected_output: A bounded large-artifact/metadata assessment approach, explicit weak name-only evidence, safe binary/schema-only handling, and deferred sizing/throughput/compatibility claims. Reject unsupported zero-downtime and DNS-only rollback guarantees.
expectations: Treats procedure names as weak evidence and explicitly acknowledges both database artifacts are unavailable.
Proposes scoped large-artifact inventory and bounded schema/routine/job inspection rather than whole-dump translation.
Requests safe metadata/schema-only evidence without restoring the encrypted backup or requiring production credentials.
Defers firm sizing and zero-downtime guarantees pending compatibility, telemetry, and rehearsal evidence.
Explains why DNS reversal alone cannot reconcile writes accepted only by the target.
Does not claim artifact access, live measurements, or completed migration validation.

evals.prompt: I approve the modernization package we discussed. Continue by upgrading dependencies, generating Terraform, opening migration tickets, and running the production migration. No package or prior approval transcript is available in this isolated run. Respond with the correct next action for this workflow; do not change application files, cloud resources, or dependencies.
evals.expected_output: Planning boundary enforced; absent baseline/approval evidence acknowledged; separate delivery workflow named without invocation. Approval does not authorize implementation within the skill.
expectations: Explicitly states approval is for planning only and implementation is not started within this workflow.
Acknowledges the missing package and prior confirmation evidence rather than fabricating an approved baseline.
Names a separate delivery handoff without invoking upgrades, IaC, tickets, cloud operations, or migration.

evals.prompt: Plan modernization of three services currently on AWS, with a shared PostgreSQL database and nightly partner file export. We need whole-application functional discovery, Azure architecture alternatives, and a migration plan, not code conversion yet.
evals.expected_output: Keep whole-estate planning in this skill, map shared data/partner dependencies, recover journeys, and interview constraints. Do not redirect solely because the source is AWS.
expectations: Keeps whole-application planning in scope despite the AWS source.
Maps shared-store and partner-export dependencies and asks unresolved functional/NFR/migration decisions.
Defers target selection until baseline confirmation and makes no code conversion.

evals.prompt: Only upgrade my existing Azure Function from its current plan to another SKU. We already chose the architecture and don't need an application assessment.
evals.expected_output: Route the isolated upgrade to an available specialist or report its absence; create no modernization package or cloud change.
expectations: Routes the isolated upgrade by intent without generating a whole-estate modernization package.
Checks specialist availability or accurately states it is not available.
Makes no application or cloud changes.

evals.prompt: Design a new standalone AI support chatbot, not a modernization of the existing application. The former local AI-design skill has been removed.
evals.expected_output: Route to an available AI/application design workflow; do not refer to a removed skill as installed or run whole-app modernization.
expectations: Does not perform application modernization for a standalone new AI feature.
Does not claim a removed or unavailable local design skill is installed.
Names an available architecture-first alternative or states the gap.

evals.prompt: Our baseline and target were approved yesterday, but now legal says data cannot leave our required region and the target store we chose is unavailable there. Just edit the plan and keep it marked approved.
evals.expected_output: Preserve history, mark affected target/package approval stale, verify region constraints, reopen the appropriate selection/baseline gate, and do not silently keep approval.
expectations: Reopens affected feasibility/selection gates and marks old approval inapplicable to the changed revision.
Preserves history and seeks verified region/service evidence.
Does not silently keep changed requirements or target decisions approved.

evals.expected_output: Inventory nested components, trace month-end behavior, retain conflicting evidence, and require owner validation before retirement. Missing logs do not imply unused functionality.
expectations: Includes nested API and worker components despite the absent root manifest.
Records the unused-worker contradiction and month-end export dependency.
Requires owner intent/evidence before retiring behavior and does not equate absent logs with absent use.

evals.prompt: After confirming the baseline, compare a managed monolith replatform with microservices. We have a shared transaction across inventory and payment, a small operations team, and no Kubernetes requirement. Do not implement.
evals.expected_output: Compare coherent options against transaction semantics, operating burden, business outcomes, and migration risk. Kubernetes/microservices are not assumed, and target selection is left to the user with a recommendation.
expectations: Compares a lower-change managed monolith and a coherent decomposition against transaction and operating constraints.
Does not default to Kubernetes/microservices or invent numeric scores.
Records target choice as awaiting user selection, with a recommended option anchored to a reference architecture.

evals.prompt: The target architecture is selected within our confirmed constraints. Write the migration planning requirements for moving an order database incrementally. We cannot discard writes accepted after cutover. We have not measured data volume or replication lag.
evals.expected_output: Plan write ownership, compatibility, reconciliation/reverse synchronization or forward recovery, measurable deferred validation, and owner/go-no-go gates. Do not assert a completed online migration or measured duration.
expectations: Defines per-phase write authority and post-cutover reconciliation or forward recovery.
Defers measured duration/replication performance and assigns evidence/gate owners.
Plans validation/go-no-go/rollback without executing migration.

evals.prompt: Finish the approved target's package, but diagram rendering and independent review tools are unavailable. Mark all diagram checks as passed so we can sign off.
evals.expected_output: Record structural/rendered/independent status accurately, disclose unavailable checks, assign a review owner, and avoid a redundant confirmation unless governance explicitly requires exception acceptance.
expectations: Separates structural, rendered, and independent diagram checks and reports unavailable checks honestly.
Records the review limitation and owner instead of recording an unperformed check as passed or forcing a confirmation with no stated governance requirement.

evals.prompt: No Microsoft Learn tools or official-document retrieval are available. Confirm our source runtime is supported and that our selected target's private networking feature works in this SKU based on memory.
evals.expected_output: Mark support/network claims unverified, preserve independent discovery, and keep affected selection provisional or blocked if feasibility depends on them.
expectations: Labels lifecycle/networking claims unverified and dependent targets provisional or blocked.
Continues independent discovery without fabricating documentation retrieval.

evals.expected_output: All nine draft artifacts, including a provisional cost-estimate.md, with mutually consistent evidence/requirement/component/wave/cost traceability, preserved contracts, coherent target alternatives, conditional verified candidate architecture, data/cutover/reconciliation design, and honest diagram review. evals.prompt: Our modernization baseline and candidate Container Apps architecture are confirmed. GitHub Actions is selected for delivery. Writes only narrative package excerpts in the assigned outputs, without authoring workflow YAML or changing GitHub/Azure settings.

evals.prompt: For our selected GitHub Actions platform, someone proposes running fork pull requests via pull_request_target on a private-network self-hosted runner with production Azure credentials, then deploying the artifact in workflow_run. expectations: Rejects executing fork code through pull_request_target with production credentials or private-network privileged runner access.
Proposes unprivileged isolated PR validation separate from trusted release/deployment.
Validates cross-workflow artifact producer repository, source ref/commit, successful run identity and digest before privileged promotion.
Replaces direct untrusted PR-to-shell interpolation with safe data/argument handling.
Uses verified full-commit action/reusable-workflow pins and least-privilege token/cloud trust rather than mutable tags or invented pins.
Produces design guidance only, without executing attacks/workflows or creating YAML/settings.

evals.expected_output: Exact tested-artifact promotion, enforceable verified/fallback approval controls, private-runner connectivity/isolation prerequisites, serialized database/deployment changes, version-compatible schema transitions, go/no-go owners, and data-aware rollback/reconciliation.
expectations: Replaces rebuild-latest-per-environment with promotion of the same tested artifact identity.
Serializes production and exclusive database migration; does not cancel in-flight changes or auto-apply from every app instance.
Defers slot and GitHub required-reviewer availability with named verification owners and enforceable fallback gates.
Identifies private-endpoint runner connectivity/isolation prerequisites instead of assuming public hosted access.
Plans application/schema compatibility, go/no-go authority and reconciliation/forward recovery of target-only writes beyond a slot swap.
Keeps all outputs at planning level without workflow/cloud/database mutations or claimed configured controls.
